title: Design Circular Deque
description:
# Design Circular Deque

Design a fixed-capacity circular double-ended queue named `MyCircularDeque`. A deque allows insertion and deletion at both the front and the rear. A circular deque must also reuse storage positions that become free after deletions, including positions at the physical beginning or end of the backing storage.

Implement the `MyCircularDeque` class:

* `MyCircularDeque(int k)` initializes the deque with capacity `k`.
* `boolean insertFront(int value)` inserts `value` at the front if the deque is not full, and returns whether the insertion succeeded.
* `boolean insertLast(int value)` inserts `value` at the rear if the deque is not full, and returns whether the insertion succeeded.
* `boolean deleteFront()` deletes the front value if the deque is not empty, and returns whether the deletion succeeded.
* `boolean deleteLast()` deletes the rear value if the deque is not empty, and returns whether the deletion succeeded.
* `int getFront()` returns the front value, or `-1` when the deque is empty.
* `int getRear()` returns the rear value, or `-1` when the deque is empty.
* `boolean isEmpty()` returns whether the deque currently has no elements.
* `boolean isFull()` returns whether the deque currently has exactly `k` elements.

Do not use a built-in deque or queue implementation. Pay particular attention to failed insertions: when the deque is already full, an insertion attempt must return `false` without changing the existing front or rear values.

In operation examples, the first array lists operations and the second lists their argument lists, paired by index and executed left to right. The first operation constructs the object; later operations use that same object. Outputs align by index too: constructors and void methods produce `null`; an empty argument list `[]` means no arguments.

## Example 1

**Input:**
["MyCircularDeque", "insertLast", "insertLast", "insertFront", "insertFront", "getRear", "isFull", "deleteLast", "insertFront", "getFront"]
[[3], [1], [2], [3], [4], [], [], [], [4], []]

**Output:**
[null, true, true, true, false, 2, true, true, true, 4]

**Explanation:**
The deque reaches capacity after inserting 1 at the rear, 2 at the rear, and 3 at the front. Inserting 4 at the front fails because the deque is full. After deleting the rear value 2, inserting 4 at the front succeeds.

## Constraints

* `1 <= k <= 1000`
* `0 <= value <= 1000`
* At most `2000` calls will be made to `insertFront`, `insertLast`, `deleteFront`, `deleteLast`, `getFront`, `getRear`, `isEmpty`, and `isFull`.

examples.output: [null, true, true, true, false, 2, true, true, true, 4]

solutions.name: Size-Tracked Circular Array
solutions.description:
## Approach
Use an array of exactly `k` slots, a `front` index, and a `size` counter. `insertFront` moves `front` one step backward before writing, while `insertLast` writes at `(front + size) % capacity`.

## Key Insight
The `size` counter is the source of truth for empty and full states. It also lets the rear position be derived from `front + size - 1`, so no separate rear pointer can drift out of sync.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(1) per operation
- Space Complexity: O(k)

solutions.name: One Empty Slot Circular Deque
solutions.description:
## Approach
Allocate `k + 1` slots and always leave one slot empty. `front` points to the current front value, and `rear` points to the next position after the current rear.

## Key Insight
This invariant avoids storing `size`: empty is `front == rear`, and full is `(rear + 1) % data.length == front`. Both front and rear insertions are pointer moves followed by a write.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(1) per operation
- Space Complexity: O(k)

solutions.name: Monotonic Index Ring Deque
solutions.description:
## Approach
Keep logical `head` and `tail` counters that may grow or shrink while physical storage is accessed through `Math.floorMod(index, capacity)`. The active deque is the half-open interval `[head, tail)`.

## Key Insight
Only array addressing needs modulo. The deque size is always `tail - head`, so inserting at the front decrements `head`, inserting at the rear increments `tail`, and both deletions move one boundary inward.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(1) per operation
- Space Complexity: O(k)

solutions.name: Sentinel Doubly Linked List
solutions.description:
## Approach
Use head and tail sentinel nodes around a doubly linked list. Inserting or deleting at either end changes only the sentinel-adjacent links, while `size` enforces capacity.

## Key Insight
Sentinels remove empty-list pointer special cases. The circular-deque capacity is still respected because every successful insertion increases `size`, and every deletion decreases it.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(1) per operation
- Space Complexity: O(k) live nodes

solutions.name: Preallocated Linked Ring Deque
solutions.description:
## Approach
Preallocate `k` linked cells in a circular doubly linked ring. `frontCell` and `rearCell` point to the current ends, and inserting at an end moves the corresponding pointer into the next free ring cell.

## Key Insight
This is the linked-node version of a circular buffer: no new nodes are allocated after construction, so repeated insert/delete cycles reuse the same storage cells forever.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(1) per operation
- Space Complexity: O(k)

tests.output: [null, true, true, true, false, 2, true, true, true, 4]

tests.description: Deque handles empty operations, full capacity, and both ends.
Capacity-one deque must update empty and full states after each end operation.
Repeated insert/delete cycles must reuse storage instead of allocating a fresh slot forever.
Front and rear remain correct after wrap-around and partial removal.
Empty and full flags must update across alternating front and rear transitions.
Failed insertions while full must not overwrite either end.
Boundary values 0 and 1000 must be preserved through both front and rear queries.
